flags.name: Flag 1 - CF Bot Management
flags.description:
In the Cloudflare console, select the one-flare.com domain, navigate to Security Rules, and open the Mitigate definite bot traffic rule. Cloudflare allows users to customize their security rules. For the Mitigate definite bot traffic rule on the one-flare.com domain, open it and see how it has been configured.
What is the response code sent after blocking? The flag is the response code.

hints.description: Custom block responses let you choose the status code.
It is the standard 'you are not allowed' code.
The flag is <s1-answer>403</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 2 - CF Security Insight
flags.description:
In the Cloudflare console, select the soledrop.co domain, open the Security dropdown and choose Security Rules, then click the Traffic Sequence button in the top right, next to Create Rule. The Traffic Sequence symbol is a circle with an arrow comming out of it and pointing to the right. Look at Security Rules for soledrop.co. The Traffic Sequence shows the simplified journey of a request as it proxies through a Cloudflare configuration.
Looking at the flow, what feature is used right before a request reaches the Origin server? The flag is the name of the box preceding Origin server

hints.description: The description of the rule is: <s1-value>to help distribute traffic between origins</s1-value>
The flag is <s1-answer>Load balancing</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 3 - CF Workers
flags.description:
While still in the Traffic Sequence window, click on Workers, select the shop-soledrop-worker from any row, choose Metrics from the nav bar at the top, and set the event window to the last 30 days. Scroll down and review the Request Distribution map. Cloudflare Workers is a serverless platform for building, deploying, and scaling apps across Cloudflare's global network without needing complex configuration. The shop.soledrop.co site from before was deployed using a custom worker. Under Request Distribution we can see the locations where a Worker ran to handle an incoming request.
Find the city where this worker was deployed the most. The flag is the name of the city.

hints.description: The <s1-label>Request Distribution</s1-label> section will have an interactable globe with pins in the locations. The flag will be the top city in the list to the right of the globe.
The flag is <s1-answer>Denver</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 4 - CF Workers AI
flags.description:
In the Cloudflare console, navigate to AI from the left-hand menu, and select Workers AI from the dropdown. In the model catalog, filter for Image Classification. Like standard Cloudflare Workers, Workers AI allow users to deploy LLMs and AI agents across Cloudflare's global network.
From the model catalog, what is the name of the model that can perform Image Classification? The flag is the name of the model

hints.description: Use the search bar to find models with <s1-value>Image Classification</s1-value> abilities.
The model is authored by <s1-value>Microsoft</s1-value>.
The flag is <s1-answer>resnet-50</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 5 - S1 AI Prompt Injection API Route
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Alerts, filter for CF-AI-PromptInjection, and open any matching alert to read the full name of the detection rule that raised it. Open a CF-AI-PromptInjection alert. The associated detection rule's name calls out the exact API route it watches. What is that route? The flag is the API route.

hints.description: The rule name ends with the route, after the words <s1-value>SoleDrop Concierge</s1-value>.
It is a versioned API path ending in the word chat.
The flag is <s1-answer>/api/v1/chat</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 6 - S1 AI Prompt Injection Attempt
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Alerts, open a CF-AI-PromptInjection alert, and read the Purple AI overview panel. According to the Purple AI overview for the CF-AI-PromptInjection alerts. A single source sending many chat POSTs in a short window is characteristic of what? The flag is the name of the attempt.

hints.description: It is automated trial-and-error against the prompt.
The word rhymes with 'buzzing'.
The flag is <s1-answer>Injection fuzzing</s1-answer>.

flags.dependsOn: Flag 5 - S1 AI Prompt Injection API Route

flags.name: Flag 7 - S1 See WAF Rule
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Hyperautomation, open the See WAF Rule workflow, and add the Cloudflare action named Get zero trust user failed logins. Read its default URL before filling in any values. In the Get zero trust user failed logins block of the See WAF Rule workflow, what is the LAST path segment of that default URL? The flag is the segment.

hints.description: The URL is a template with unfilled placeholders like <s1-value>account_id</s1-value>.
It is the very end of the path, after the user id — two words joined by an underscore.
The flag is <s1-answer>failed_logins</s1-answer>.

flags.dependsOn: Flag 6 - S1 AI Prompt Injection Attempt

flags.name: Flag 8 - S1 Default URL
flags.description:
In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Hyperautomation, open the See WAF Rule workflow, and open the Cloudflare action named Get zero trust user failed logins. Copy the default URL for the Get zero trust user failed logins action, paste it into a browser exactly as-is with the placeholders still in it, and press enter.
What is the error message in the JSON body? The flag is the error message.
flags.plainAnswer: Could not route to /client/v4/accounts/account_id/access/users/user_id/failed_logins, perhaps your object identifier is invalid?

hints.description: Cloudflare's API rejects the unfilled placeholders as invalid object identifiers.
The message begins with <s1-value>Could not route to ...</s1-value> and ends by questioning your object identifier.
The flag is <s1-answer>Could not route to /client/v4/accounts/account_id/access/users/user_id/failed_logins, perhaps your object identifier is invalid?</s1-answer>.
